transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, Doc, I’m mostly here because of what’s going on at work. I'm a transportation inspector, and ever since I won this county safety award... which, honestly, the whole banquet they threw for that was a total joke. They hired this cheap catering company and the chicken was completely raw in the middle. My buddy Dave was out for three days sick, and he’s the guy who usually checks the hydraulics on the heavy rigs, so that backed the whole yard up for a week. 

But anyway, ever since I got that award, certain people at the office have been twisting my inspection reports. They keep asking these really pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked or something. And my supervisor just brushes it off, says it’s just a normal review. Normal review. Have you ever tried to get a straight answer out of county admin? Took me four months just to get a new reflective vest last year because of their "normal" paperwork, so I know how they operate. But I can tell what's really happening. Even with him saying that, I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.
Do you believe that certain people at work are intentionally trying to harm or undermine you, even though there's no clear evidence to support that belief?

Well, when you say "no clear evidence," that's just... I mean, I just told you what they're doing. The evidence is right in front of them. Ever since I got that safety award, they are absolutely twisting my inspection reports around. They keep bringing up the budget, asking these really specific, pointed questions to try and make me look crooked. 

Which is rich, honestly, because if you want to talk about the budget, you should see the new street sweepers the county just bought. Absolute garbage. They break down every twenty miles. I told the procurement guy, I said, "You're buying from the wrong vendor," but nobody listens to the guys on the ground. My buddy Mike used to drive sweepers before he hurt his back—slipped on some ice outside a gas station, actually, messed up his lower back pretty bad. He’s been fighting the insurance company for like two years. It's a total nightmare, he can't even pick up his kids right now. 

But yeah, my supervisor looks at me and says, "Oh, it's just a normal review." Normal review, my eye. I can tell there is a completely coordinated effort to discredit me. They want me gone, no matter what he says.
Do you think others are trying to harm or undermine you outside of work, or is this something that you believe is only happening in your workplace?

No, no, it's... it's just the guys at the office. Outside of work, I don't really have those kinds of problems. I mean, my neighbors are fine. Well, mostly fine. The guy next door, Stan, he just got this new riding mower, one of those zero-turn ones? And he mows his lawn at like seven in the morning on Saturdays. I mean, who does that? I work all week, sometimes I'm out at the weigh stations till past midnight if there's a backup on the interstate. Last month, we had this massive pileup near exit 42 because some guy fell asleep at the wheel of a rig hauling frozen chickens. Took us fourteen hours to clear the road. You wouldn't believe the smell once the sun came up and those things started thawing on the asphalt. It was unbelievable. 

But anyway, yeah, Stan's annoying with the mower, but he's not out to get me or anything. It's really just the people at the county office. They're the ones messing with my reports. Outside of that, things are pretty normal.
Do you feel certain that your coworkers are trying to undermine you, even if they or others have not directly admitted to it or provided proof?

I am absolutely certain. I mean, they don't have to admit it, do they? You don't need someone to hand you a signed confession when they're literally twisting your inspection reports right in front of you. Ever since I got that county safety award, it's been non-stop. They keep asking these pointed budget questions, trying to make me look crooked. 

And you know, speaking of the budget, they just cut our overtime pay again. Said it was a "necessary reallocation of funds." Reallocation, right. They spent thirty grand on remodeling the breakroom downtown. They put in this fancy espresso machine that nobody even knows how to use. My buddy Carl tried to make a cappuccino last week and the thing basically exploded, shot hot milk all over his uniform. He had to go do a commercial vehicle inspection smelling like burnt dairy. The trucker he pulled over thought he was drunk, kept asking him to take a breathalyzer. Carl was so mad, he almost quit right there.

But yeah, my supervisor, he just sits there and says it's a "normal review." Normal review. I'm not stupid. I can tell there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. They're not going to admit it, but I know exactly what they're doing.

Do you believe that the people at the office trying to discredit you are acting on their own, or do you think they’re following orders from someone or something bigger, like a government agency or a secret group?

No, no, I don't think it's the CIA or the FBI or anything crazy like that. It's not some secret group. It's just my supervisor and the guys in the office acting on their own. I mean, the federal government, like the federal DOT guys, they don't even care about our little county office. 

Last time a federal auditor came down, he didn't even look at the trucks. He just sat in his rental car eating a sandwich. It was a Chevy Malibu, one of those newer ones with the weird front grill. My cousin Derek had a Malibu back in maybe 2018, but he traded it in for a Tacoma because he wanted to start a landscaping business. He bought all these mowers and edgers on credit, but then it rained for like three weeks straight that spring and he couldn't get any yards done. He ended up having to sell the whole lot on Craigslist just to make rent. It was a huge mess, his girlfriend was so mad at him she went and stayed with her sister in Ohio for a month. 

But yeah, anyway, there's no big government conspiracy or anything. It's just the guys at work being petty and trying to push me out because they're jealous of my award.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others around you don't seem to notice, like voices or visions?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or see ghosts or whatever. My hearing is perfectly normal. Well, actually, it's probably better than normal just because of the job. You have to have a good ear. I can hear a bad axle bearing from like fifty yards away. 

Just last Tuesday, this guy pulled up to the scales in an old Freightliner, and I heard this awful high-pitched squealing sound. I told him to pull off to the side, and sure enough, his front right bearing was completely shot. He was hauling a full load of watermelons, all the way up from Florida. Can you imagine if that wheel locked up on the interstate at sixty miles an hour? Just... watermelons everywhere. Smashed all over the road. 

I do love a good watermelon, though. My grandma used to grow them in her backyard when I was a kid. She had this massive garden out back—tomatoes, squash, sweet corn, everything. But the deer kept coming out of the woods and eating the tops off the plants, so my grandpa spent three whole weekends building this eight-foot fence out of chicken wire and old shipping pallets. He actually hit his thumb with a hammer on the second day. Hit it so hard the nail turned completely black and just fell off a few weeks later. It looked really gross. He had to wrap it in electrical tape because he couldn't find any band-aids in the garage and didn't want to track mud into the house to get one. 

But... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about the weigh station?
Do you believe, without any doubt, that these people at work are deliberately and repeatedly trying to harm or ruin you, even though they may not have any real reason to do so?

Yeah, without a doubt. I mean, they don't have a real reason, except they're just jealous. Like I said, it all started right after I got that county safety award. Ever since then, they've been twisting my inspection reports, asking all these pointed budget questions. They're trying to make me look crooked, like I'm doing something shady with the numbers. My supervisor just sits there and calls it a "normal review," but I know it's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

Speaking of reviews, I had to get my truck inspected last week. The guy at the shop tried to tell me I needed all new brake pads and rotors. I told him, buddy, I'm a transportation inspector, I know what a worn rotor looks like. He got all defensive, started waving his little flashlight around. It was one of those really bright tactical flashlights, the kind they advertise on TV that they say can blind a bear or whatever. My brother-in-law bought one of those for a camping trip up in the mountains. He said he was going to use it to spot raccoons, but he ended up just dropping it in a creek on the first night. He tried to dry it out in a bag of rice, like you do with a cell phone, but it never worked right after that. The light would just flicker randomly. He finally got so annoyed he threw it in the trash. 

But yeah, they're definitely out to ruin me at work. I can see right through what they're doing.
Do you believe that your coworkers’ attempts to discredit you are part of a larger pattern or scheme that others would not normally notice or understand?

Yeah, I mean, absolutely. They think they're being so slick, but I see the pattern. Anyone else would just think it's normal office politics, like, "Oh, they're just checking the budget," but I know it's a whole scheme they've put together. They do it in these little ways that don't look obvious unless you're the one getting targeted. 

It's like when you're looking at a bad weld on a trailer frame. If you just glance at it, it looks fine, just a little bumpy maybe. But if you really look close, you see the stress fractures starting to spiderweb out. I saw one like that a couple months ago on a flatbed hauling lumber. The guy had it strapped down with these cheap, frayed neon orange ratchet straps. I hate those orange ones. They always fade in the sun after like two weeks and turn this ugly peach color. My neighbor used to have a peach tree in his front yard, right by the sidewalk. Every summer, the peaches would drop and rot on the concrete, and there would be thousands of yellow jackets just swarming the whole block. I got stung right on the back of the neck while I was mowing my lawn one time. Had to put a paste made of baking soda and water on it. My mom taught me that trick when I was a kid. She kept this giant yellow box of baking soda under the sink that seemed like it lasted for ten years. She used it for everything—cleaning the oven, making cookies, getting the smell out of my hockey gear. 

But yeah, the pattern is definitely there. They're trying to build a case against me, piece by piece, and they think I'm too stupid to notice.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, unfounded belief that coworkers are intentionally trying to discredit him without any evidence of delusions or hallucinations, and the symptoms are limited to the workplace. The lack of bizarre content, absence of other psychotic features, and circumscribed nature of the delusion supports the diagnosis of Delusional Disorder, Somatic Type, although the predominant theme aligns more specifically with the jealous/persecutory subtype. However, the ICD-10 code F22.0 (Persistent Delusional Disorders) is the most accurate based on the patient's chronic, non-bizarre delusions of persecution confined to a specific context.
